answer: Agents trading saffron from an orchard near a coastal inlet must lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before each identity can submit bids, with one active bid per identity. The escrow contract enforces the same lock for every new account, so creating names is cheap but gaining bidding capacity is not: an attacker using 10,000 identities must immobilize $1 million for a month, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital.
